abstract: Synapsin associates with synaptic vesicles. How these local contacts give rise to a connected vesicle assembly remains unclear. We used a three-dimensional Brownian agent model to vary electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions independently at fixed particle abundance and confinement. With electrostatics alone, the agents representing synapsin approached almost every vesicle early, when most vesicles still belonged to separate groups. With both interactions active, a larger connected assembly formed earlier, more of these agents were near several vesicles, and they moved more slowly. Over the full 84 ms, the assemblies continued to grow under either interaction alone. By the final observation window, the two conditions had similar vesicle participation despite differences in protein association and contact composition. The positive early interaction contrast decreased as the assemblies grew. These observations distinguish local synapsin association from collective vesicle connectivity and identify a structural feature that can be measured alongside condensate formation.
